source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 134: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: Assumptions for variant 134: hold the model/tokenizer, precision, runtime build, hardware, serving policy, autoscaling, and a versioned mix of short prompts and long generations fixed; report measured values with units and do not infer platform-specific behavior. Test the falsifiable hypothesis that the candidate scheduling/admission policy increases goodput by at least 5% at the declared offered load, while queue-inclusive P99 end-to-end latency is no more than 10% above baseline and correctness is non-inferior under variant 134. Use a randomized paired crossover: replay the same seeded requests under baseline and candidate in counterbalanced order, isolate background load, declare warm-up and discard it, and repeat independent trials to a prespecified confidence/precision target or safety stopping rule. Capture per-request arrival, queue entry/exit, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token, each decode step, completion, cancellation, timeout, and error timestamps. Define TTFT as arrival-to-first-token and separately publish service-only TTFT; define TPOT with its generated-token denominator and state whether the first-token interval is excluded. Report request/token throughput, goodput numerator and denominator, queue-time distribution, and P99 end-to-end latency, stratified by input length, output length, concurrency, and burstiness; separate prefill from decode. Collect GPU utilization/memory/KV-cache occupancy, CPU, power, temperature/throttling, cache state, OOMs, timeouts, cancellations, and correctness/failure outcomes. Control or log cache warming, request mix, arrival-rate drift, batching, scheduler settings, background work, thermal state, and measurement overhead. Require a versioned manifest, raw lifecycle traces, paired trial assignments, metric definitions, stratum counts, uncertainty intervals, and failure logs. Roll back or stop the candidate on error/correctness regression, OOMs, thermal throttling, or the declared P99 safety breach; otherwise do not claim improvement unless the prespecified effect and uncertainty criteria are met.
risks: Queue-inclusive and service-only latency can be conflated.
Request mix, cache state, arrival drift, or background load can invalidate paired comparisons.
P99/goodput and correctness conclusions are unstable without fixed denominators, strata, repetitions, and stopping rules.
Synthetic workload results may not generalize to production traffic.
evidence_required: Versioned model/runtime/hardware/workload manifest and candidate configuration.
Randomized paired trial logs with warm-up policy, stratum counts, metric denominators, and uncertainty estimates.
Request lifecycle traces, prefill/decode timings, resource/thermal/KV telemetry, and correctness/failure logs.
